The term successors as used herein shall include any corporation or other business entity which shall, whether by merger, consolidation, purchase, or otherwise, acquire all or substantially all of the business and assets of the Bank or of an Eligible Affiliate, and the successors of any such corporation or other business entity. 10 Article VI. Amendment and Termination. 6.1 Amended and Termination (a) Amendment or Termination of the Plan. The Bank and Eligible Affiliates expect to continue the Plan indefinitely, but specifically reserve the right, in the sole and unfettered discretion of the Bank's Board of Directors, at any time, to amend, in whole or in part, any or all of the provisions of the Plan and to terminate the Plan in whole or in part, provided, however, that no such amendment or termination shall adversely affect any rights of an Outside Director to receive the Retirement Benefit which had accrued on their behalf on account of their service as an Outside Director prior to such amendment or termination or of a retired or former Outside Director to continue to receive benefits accrued for such person hereunder. Any termination of the Plan that results in accelerated payment of benefits shall comply with the requirements of Section 6.1(b) hereof. (b) Requirements for Termination. The Bank may, in its discretion, elect to terminate the Plan in any of the following three circumstances below and accelerate the payment of the entire unpaid balance or payment of the Participant's benefit as if the Participant had Separated from Service as of the date of the Plan termination and in accordance with Section 409A of the Code: (i) the Plan is irrevocably terminated by Board action within the 30 days preceding a Change in Control (as defined in Treasury Regulation 1.409A-3(i)(5)) and (i) all arrangements sponsored by the Bank that would be aggregated with the Plan under Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1 (c)(2) are terminated, and (ii) the Participant and all participants under the other aggregated arrangements receive all of their benefits under the terminated arrangements within 12 months of the date the Bank irrevocably takes all necessary action to terminate the Plan and the other aggregated arrangements; (ii) the Plan is irrevocably terminated at a time that is not proximate to a downturn in the financial health of the Bank and (i) all arrangements sponsored by the Bank that would be aggregated with the Plan under Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1(c) if the Participant participated in such arrangements are terminated, (ii) no payments are made within 12 months of the date the Bank takes all necessary action to irrevocably terminate the arrangements, other than payments that would be payable under the terms of the arrangements if the termination had not occurred, (iii) all payments are made within 24 months of the date the Bank takes all necessary 11 action to irrevocably terminate the arrangements, and (iv) the Bank does not adopt a new arrangement that would be aggregated with the Plan under Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1(c) if a Participant participated in both arrangements, at any time within three years following the date the Bank takes all necessary action to irrevocably terminate the Plan; or (iii) the Plan is terminated within 12 months of a corporate dissolution taxed under Section 331 of the Code, or with the approval of a bankruptcy court pursuant to 11 U.S.C. §503(b)(1)(A), provided that the amounts deferred by a Participant under the Plan are included in the Participant's gross income in the later of (i) the calendar year in which the termination of the Plan occurs, or (ii) the first calendar year in which the payment is administratively practicable. 6.2 Subject to Regulatory Action and Compliance with Code Section 409A The Plan shall be effective until and unless it is found to violate any rule or regulation of any governmental agency which is authorized to regulate the Bank, Eligible Affiliate, or the Plan, or fail to comply with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code, in which case the Plan shall be terminated as of the date of violation, or amended to the extent necessary to avoid the violation of any rule or regulation of a governmental agency authorized to regulate the Bank, Eligible Affiliate, or the Plan, or to comply with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code in order to preserve the tax-deferred treatment of the Benefits accrued under the Plan pending distribution to Participants. No distribution shall be made from the Plan or action taken under the Plan that would make any Retirement Benefit payable or accrued hereunder subject to the interest and additional tax imposed by Code Section 409A(a)(1)(6). IN WITNESS WHEREOF, Northwest Bank has caused this Amended and Restated Retirement Plan for Outside Directors, to be executed by its duly authorized officers on the date set forth below, effective as of December 31, 2026. NORTHWEST BANK November 19, 2026 By: /s/ Erin F. Siegfried Date Erin F. Siegfried Chief Legal Counsel 31461803.2

title: Northwest Bancshares, Inc.
text: EX-10.2 3 northwestbanksupplementa.htm EX-10.2 northwestbanksupplementa - 1 - NORTHWEST SAVINGS BANK NONQUALIFIED SUPPLEMENTAL RETIREMENT PLAN Preamble Northwest Bank, formally known as Northwest Mutual Savings Association, doing business as Northwest Savings Bank (“Employer”), established the Northwest Savings Bank Pension Plan as a defined benefit pension plan (“Qualified Plan”) intended to be qualified under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (“Code”), for the purpose of providing income to its employees during their retirement from their service with the Bank. Sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code reduce the pension otherwise payable under the Northwest Savings Bank Pension Plan to employees whose compensation exceeds the limits of Section 401(a)(17) or for whom contributions or benefits would exceed the limits of Section 415. Effective June 16, 1993, the Employer established this supplemental retirement plan of unfunded deferred compensation that is not qualified under the Code (“Nonqualified Plan”) to make up for the cut back in retirement income required by the above-referred Sections of the Code with respect to senior higher paid employees who retire on or after the Earliest Retirement Age provided under the Qualified Plan. This Nonqualified Plan provides a supplemental retirement benefit for participants in the Northwest Savings Bank Pension Plan which, when combined with the pension payable to them under the Qualified Plan, will equal the pension which they would have received thereunder but for the application of Section 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code. Effective January 1, 2006, this Nonqualified Plan was amended and restated in its entirety to comply with Section 409A of the Code. Effective August 1, 2020, this Nonqualified - 2 - Plan was amended again to implement a soft freeze of the Plan so that only those Employees who were Participants on or before July 31, 2020, would be eligible to participate in this Nonqualified Plan after July 31, 2020. Effective January 1, 2023, this Nonqualified Plan was amended and restated in its entirety to update the Nonqualified Plan; and it is being further amended and restated effective as of the close of business on December 31, 2026, to freeze all benefit accruals as of December 31, 2026. No amendment or restatement has modified in any way the form or time of payment of amounts deferred before such amendment or restatement. ARTICLE I Definitions 1.1. Incorporation by Reference. Unless the context of this Plan requires or connotes a different meaning, all undefined capitalized terms used in this Plan shall have the same meanings as are respectively assigned to them under the Northwest Savings Bank Pension Plan (“Qualified Plan”), and the terms and conditions of the Qualified Plan are incorporated herein by reference wherever necessary or appropriate. 1.2. “Benefit Formula” means the method set forth in the Qualified Plan to calculate the amount of benefit payable to a participant thereunder at the time such benefit commences to be paid, including all actuarially equivalent factors utilized under the Qualified Plan, and excluding any actuarial adjustment for the postponement of the commencement of Retirement Benefits payable to any Participant after their 70th birthday. As Amended effective 7/1/2002, the Benefit Formula shall include all applicable actuarial reductions, and all offsets and deductions, required by the Qualified Plan for payments available from Federal Social Security, from Worker’s Compensation, and from other qualified plans, if any, but shall not reflect the application of sections 401(a)(17) or 415 of the Code. - 3 - 1.3. “Effective Date” means June 16, 1993. 1.4. “Participant” means a participant in the Qualified Plan, or the beneficiary or estate of a deceased Participant, who is or becomes entitled to a benefit hereunder by reason of a reduction required by Sections 401(a)(17) or 415 of the Code in the amount of benefit otherwise payable to such Participant as a participant in the Qualified Plan, or to their beneficiary or estate, if deceased. Effective January 1, 2006, “Participant” means an Employee who the Committee specifies to be a Participant in this Plan in accordance with Section 3.1, and the beneficiary or estate of any such Participant who is deceased. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Participant does not include any individual who had not been participating in this Nonqualified Plan before August 1, 2020. 1.5. “Committee” means the members of the Employer’s Board of Directors appointed to administer this Plan. 1.6. “Supplemental Retirement Benefit” means the benefit payable by the Company to a Participant hereunder. 1.7. “Nonqualified Plan” means the Northwest Savings Bank Nonqualified Supplemental Retirement Plan as herein set forth and as it may hereafter be amended from time to time. 1.8. “Payment Event” is defined in Section 2.2 hereof. 1.9. “Qualified Plan” means the Northwest Savings Bank Pension Plan, a defined benefit pension plan sponsored by the Employer for the benefit of its eligible employees, which is or is intended to be qualified under Section 401 of the Code, as the Qualified Plan presently exists, and as it may be hereafter amended, superseded, modified, or redesignated. - 4 - ARTICLE II Calculation and Payment of Supplemental Retirement Benefit 2.1. Amount of Supplemental Retirement Benefit. The Supplemental Retirement Benefit payable to a Participant hereunder shall equal the difference between the amount payable to the Participant as a participant under the Qualified Plan and the amount which would have been payable to such participant after the Effective Date under the Benefit Formula of the Qualified Plan but for the limitations of Sections 401(a)(17) or 415 of the Code, as such Sections may be amended from time to time hereafter, or under any successor provisions of such Sections. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, effective as of the close of business on December 31, 2026 (the “Participation Freeze Date”), no Participant shall accrue any additional Supplemental Retirement Benefit under the Plan. For purposes of determining the Supplemental Retirement Benefit payable under this Section 2.1, only Compensation, credited service, and other benefit- determining factors recognized under the Qualified Plan through December 31, 2026 shall be taken into account. No Compensation earned, service performed, or other benefit-determining factor attributable to periods after December 31, 2026 shall be recognized for any purpose under this Plan. Each Participant's accrued Supplemental Retirement Benefit shall be determined and frozen as of the Participation Freeze Date. Benefits accrued through December 31, 2026 shall remain payable in the same form and at the same time as provided under the terms of the Plan, as in effect immediately prior to the Participation Freeze Date. - 5 - 2.2. Form and Time of Payment of Supplemental Retirement Benefit Six Months Following A Payment Event. The Supplemental Retirement Benefit of a Participant hereunder shall be in the form of the lump sum actuarial equivalent of the amount calculated under Section 2.1, payable in accordance with one of the three options that the Participant shall elect pursuant to Section 2.3 on or before December 31, 2006, or within thirty (30) days of becoming eligible to participate in this Plan after 2006. Payment in accordance with the option elected shall be made or commenced after a waiting period of six months following the first to occur of the following Payment Events: the Participant’s death, Total and Permanent Disability, Retirement Date or a change in the ownership or effective control of the Employer and its Affiliated Employers, or a change in the ownership of a substantial portion of the assets of the Employer and its Affiliated Employers (as such changes are defined in Regulations issued by the Secretary of the Treasury under Code Section 409A). 2.3. Participant’s Election of Method and Time of Payment. Within thirty (30) days of becoming eligible to participate in this Plan, or by December 31, 2006 in the case of any Participant in the Plan in 2006, the Participant shall deliver to the Plan Administrator their election of one of the following three (3) options for payment of the lump sum actuarial equivalent of the amount of compensation deferred under the Qualified Plan calculated under Section 2.1, but reduced by the amount of any compensation deferred with respect to the services which the Participant performed after 2006 and prior to the Participant’s delivery of their election to the Plan Administrator: (a) Lump sum payable on the date which follows the occurrence of the first Payment Event by six months; (b) Three (3) substantially equal annual installments, the first of which is payable on the date which follows the occurrence of the first Payment Event by - 6 - six months, the second and third installments of which are payable on the second and third anniversaries of the payment of the first installment; or (c) Five (5) substantially equal annual installments, the first of which is payable on the date which follows the occurrence of the first Payment Event by six months, the second through fifth installments of which are respectively payable on the second through fifth anniversaries of the payment of the first installment. Each of the substantially equal annual installments available under payment options (b) and (c) is hereby designated a separate payment and shall bear interest at the annual earnings rate paid on the Bank’s five (5) year certificates of deposit as of the end of the preceding fiscal year, from the date of the Payment Event which entitles the Participant to receive or commence receiving benefits under this Nonqualified Plan to the date of actual distribution of Plan benefits to the Participant. If the Participant fails to deliver their method and payment election to the Plan Administrator within 30 days of becoming eligible to participate in the Plan the Participant shall be deemed to have elected option (c) above, payment in five (5) substantially equal annual installments. 2.4. Participant’s Option to Defer Payment of Any Installment of the Supplemental Retirement Benefit For At Least 5 Years. A Participant may elect to defer the payment of the lump sum or any one or more of the three (3) or five (5) separate annual installments of the Supplemental Retirement Benefit scheduled to be paid to the Participant in accordance with the payment election which the participant made pursuant to Section 2.3 following the occurrence of the earliest of the four Payment Events listed in Section 2.2 for at least five (5) years beyond the respective dates of payment scheduled in accordance with Section 2.3 by delivering their written - 7 - election to defer to the Plan Administrator at least 12 months prior to the occurrence of any of the Payment Events listed in Section 2.2. The Participant must specify in such written election the lump sum payment or which one or more of the three (3) or five (5) separate annual installments the Participant elects to defer, and the elected date of deferred payment, which must be not earlier than the fifth anniversary of the date of payment previously scheduled pursuant to Section 2.3. There is no limit on the number of deferral elections which a Participant may execute with respect to the lump sum payment or each of the three (3) or five (5) separate annual installments of the Supplemental Retirement Benefit scheduled to be paid in accordance with Section 2.3, provided that each deferral election is delivered to the Plan Administrator at least 12 months prior to occurrence of any of the Payment Events listed in Section 2.2, and provided further that each deferral election with respect to any installment defers payment of that installment for at least 5 years beyond the previously scheduled payment date. All deferral elections which a Participant may deliver pursuant to this Section 2.4 are irrevocable, subject to the limited exceptions provided by this Section 2.4. 2.5. Contingent Nature of Supplemental Retirement Benefit. The Supplemental Retirement Benefit payable to any Participant hereunder is contingent only and is subject to forfeiture upon the occurrence of any of the conditions or for any of the reasons provided in Section 3.2 at all times prior to being distributed to or vested in each Participant in accordance with the orders of the Committee given pursuant to Section 3.3. 2.6. Aggregate Benefit Limitation. This Nonqualified Plan shall not be construed or applied as providing for payments to any Participant which, when combined with benefits payable under the Qualified Plan, exceed the amounts payable to or on behalf of such Participant as a participant under the Benefit Formula of the Qualified Plan apart from the limitations of Sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code. This Nonqualified Plan shall not be a substitute for or - 8 - an alternative to the Qualified Plan, which shall remain the primary source of all benefits provided thereunder. 2.7. Employer’s Right to Delay Scheduled Payment of Supplemental Retirement Benefit Under Certain Circumstances. The Employer has the right to delay making a payment of Supplemental Retirement Benefit scheduled to be paid to any Participant (or the beneficiary or estate of any Participant) under Sections 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 in the event that, and to the extent that, in the Employer’s reasonable opinion, such scheduled payment will: (a) violate a term or covenant of a loan agreement or similar agreement to which the Employer is a party, which the Employer entered into for legitimate business reasons, and not to avoid the restrictions on deferral elections under Code Section 409A, and such violation will cause material harm to the Employer; or (b) not be deductible by the Employer under Code Section 162(m); or (c) violate Federal securities laws or other applicable law; or (d) jeopardize the solvency of the Employer; then, following the occurrence and passage of any of such events which in the Employer’s reasonable opinion justifies a delay in payment, the payment shall be made as soon as the event justifying the delay no longer exists, or in the case of a payment which is delayed to avoid an anticipated violation of Code §162(m), the payment shall be made in the calendar year in which the Participant separates from service. 2.8. Acceleration of Payment of Supplemental Retirement Benefit for Payment of Participant’s Taxes. Payment of the Supplemental Retirement Benefit calculated under Section - 9 - 2.1 which is scheduled to be paid in accordance with Sections 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 hereof shall be automatically accelerated to the extent necessary to pay: (a) taxes imposed on any Participant’s Supplemental Retirement Benefit under the Federal Insurance Contributions Act (Code Sections 3101, 3121(a) and 3121(v)(2) (“FICA”)), and to pay the income tax at the source on wages imposed under Code Section 3401 or the corresponding withholding provisions of applicable state, local or foreign tax laws as a result of the payment of the FICA taxes imposed on any Participant’s Supplemental Retirement Benefit; and (b) all amounts required to be included in any Participant’s income at any time when this Nonqualified Plan and the Supplemental Retirement Benefit accrued hereunder for any Participant fails to meet the requirements of Code Section 409A and the regulations promulgated thereunder. ARTICLE III Designation of Participants Entitled to Benefits; Forfeiture of Benefits 3.1. Designation of Participants Entitled to Benefits. The Committee shall specify which Employee who is a participant in the Qualified Plan whose compensation exceeds the limitations of Code Sections 401(a)(17) and 415 in any calendar year shall be a Participant in this Nonqualified Plan with respect to Compensation earned in that calendar year. The Committee shall deliver prompt written notice to each Employee who it specifies to be a Participant in this Nonqualified Plan. The Committee shall advise each Employee who it specifies to be a Participant in this Plan of their obligation to make a payment election pursuant to Section 2.3 - 10 - within 30 days of such written notice. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, participation in the Plan shall be frozen as of July 31, 2020. No Employee who is not a Participant in the Plan on July 31, 2020, shall become a Participant in the Plan on or after August 1, 2020. 3.2. Forfeitures of Benefits. The contingent right of a Participant to receive future payments hereunder shall be forfeited upon the occurrence of any one or more of the following events: (a) if the Participant is discharged from employment by the Employer for an act which, in the opinion of the Committee, constitutes fraud against, or embezzlement of funds of, the Employer or its customers; or (b) if the Participant shall enter into a business or employment which the Committee determines to be (i) detrimentally competitive with the business of the Employer, and (ii) substantially damaging to the Employer’s financial interests; or (c) if the Participant terminates employment with the Employer prior to their Earliest Retirement Age, death, or Total and Permanent Disability or prior to a change in the ownership or effective control of the Employer, as defined in Regulations issued by the Secretary of the Treasury. ARTICLE IV Plan Administration 4.1. Duties and Obligations of Committee. Responsibility to administer this Plan and to interpret and carry out its provisions is hereby delegated to the Committee comprised of - 11 - members of the Employer’s Board of Directors who are appointed to administer this Plan. The Committee shall appoint one of its members or a member of the Employer’s Human Resources Department to be the Plan Administrator. The Committee and its delegates shall have the same rights, powers, duties, and fiduciary obligations, and operate with the same standard of care, with respect to this Plan and its Participants as the Plan Administrator of the Qualified Plan has and does with respect to the Qualified Plan and its participants. 4.2. Eligibility and Benefit Determination. The Committee shall have the sole right to determine the eligibility of any person to participate in this Plan, and the amount of any benefit payable hereunder; provided, however, that any such determination shall be made under uniform rules consistently applied to persons in like circumstances. Any designation of a beneficiary or revocation of same made by a Participant under the Qualified Plan shall apply with equal force and effect to this Nonqualified Plan. ARTICLE V. Funding 5.1. Unfunded, Nonqualified Plan. The Employer shall not be required to establish any form or trust or funded account for the purpose of providing any Supplemental Retirement Benefit. The Nonqualified Plan is intended to be a plan that is not qualified within the meaning of Code Section 401(a) and that "is unfunded and is maintained by an employer primarily for the purpose of providing deferred compensation for a select group of management or highly compensated employees" within the meaning of ERISA. The Plan - 12 - will be administered and interpreted to the extent possible in a manner consistent with that intent. 5.2. Optional Funding. In order to meet its contingent deferred obligations here under, the Employer may set aside or earmark funds in an amount necessary to actuarially fund part or all of the total retirement benefits expect to be paid from this Plan under Article II. Funds set aside or earmarked to meet the Employer’s contingent deferred obligation hereunder may be kept in cash, or invested and reinvested, in the discretion of the Committee. Title to and beneficial ownership of any assets, whether cash or investments, which the Employer may set aside or earmark to meet its contingent, deferred obligations hereunder, shall at all times remain in the Employer; and no Participant or beneficiary shall under any circumstances acquire any property interest in any specific assets of the Employer. 5.3. Investment of Earmarked Funds. Investments of funds set aside or earmarked to meet the Employer’s contingent deferred obligation hereunder may be made in savings accounts, stocks, bonds, or other securities selected by the Committee in its sole discretion. In the exercise of the foregoing discretionary investment powers, the Committee may engage investment counsel, and, if it so desires, may delegate to such counsel full or limited authority to select the securities in which the funds are to be invested. The cost of any such service shall be charged as an expense of administering the Plan and paid as provided in Section 6.2. - 13 - ARTICLE VI General 6.1. Inducement to Employees Affected by Limitations of Code Sections 401(a)(17) and 415. This Nonqualified Supplemental Retirement Plan is adopted in consideration of the valuable contributions to the Employer made by Participants whose benefits otherwise available from the Employer’s Qualified Plans have been reduced by application of Sections 401(a)(17) and 415 of the Code and with the intention that the provision of this Plan shall be disseminated to all such Participants so that it may act as an inducement to them to continue to devote their utmost efforts, leadership and counsel in the service of the best interests of the Employer over the long term with a sense of security regarding the amount of retirement benefit which they may rely upon for income following the conclusion of their career with the Employer. 6.2. Expenses. The books and records to be maintained for the purpose of the Nonqualified Plan shall be maintained by the officers and employees of the Employer at its expense and subject to the supervision and control of the Committee. All expenses of administering the Nonqualified Plan shall be paid by the Employer either from funds set aside or earmarked under the Plan or from other funds. 6.3. Prohibition Against Assignment of Benefits. To the extent permitted by law, the right of any Participant or any beneficiary in any benefit or to any payment hereunder shall not be subject in any manner to attachment or other legal process for the debts of such Participant or beneficiary; and any such benefit or payment shall not be subject to anticipation, alienation, sale, transfer, assignment, or encumbrance. However, the rights of a Participant - 14 - hereunder may be subject to the terms of a domestic relations order as defined in Code Section 414(p)(1)(B) issued by a Court having jurisdiction over the Participant for support of the Participant’s spouse, former spouse or dependent. 6.4. No Liability for Actions Taken in Good Faith. No member of the Board of Directors of the Employer or of the Committee and no officer or employee of the Employer shall be liable to any person for any action taken or omitted in connection with the administration of this Nonqualified Plan unless attributable to his own fraud of willful misconduct; nor shall the Employer be liable to any person for any such action unless attributable to fraud or willful misconduct on the part of the director, officer, or employee of the Employer. 6.5. No Contract of Employment. This Nonqualified Plan shall not be construed to establish a guarantee of future or continued employment by the Employer of any Participant. 6.6. No Trust or Fiduciary Relationship Created. Nothing contained herein shall be deemed to create a trust of any kind or create any fiduciary relationship. Funds invested hereunder shall continue for all purposes to be a part of the general funds of the Employer, will remain, the general, unpledged, and unrestricted assets of the Employer, and no person other than the Employer shall, by virtue of the provisions of this Nonqualified Plan, have any interest in such funds. To the extent that any person acquires a right to receive payments from the Employer under this Nonqualified Plan, such right shall be no greater than the right of any unsecured general creditor of the Employer. An Employer's obligation under this Nonqualified Plan will be merely that of an unfunded and unsecured promise to pay money in the future. 6.7. Incompetency of a Participant or Beneficiary. If the Committee determines that any person entitled to payments under the Nonqualified Plan is an infant or - 15 - incompetent by reason of physical or mental disability, it may cause all payments thereafter becoming due to such person to be made to any other person for his benefit, without responsibility to follow application of amounts so paid. Payments made pursuant to this provision shall completely discharge the Employer, the Nonqualified Plan, and the Committee. 6.8. Applicable Law and Construction. The provisions of the Nonqualified Plan shall be construed, administered, and governed under the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania to the extent such laws are not preempted by ERISA or any other federal laws which may from time to time be applicable. Whenever any words are used herein in the singular form, they shall be construed as though they were also used in the plural form in all cases where they would so apply. Titles of Articles and Sections hereof are for convenience of reference only and are not to be taken into account in construing the provisions of this Plan. 6.9. Severability. In case any provision of the Nonqualified Plan shall be held illegal or invalid for any reason, said illegality or invalidity shall not affect the remaining parts of the Nonqualified Plan, which shall be construed and enforced as if said illegal and invalid provision had never been inserted herein. 6.10 Section 409A. The terms of the Nonqualified Plan and its operation are intended to comply with Section 409A of the Code. The Nonqualified Plan shall be administered, interpreted, and construed in a manner consistent with Section 409A of the Code. Notwithstanding anything in the Nonqualified Plan to the contrary, distributions under the Nonqualified Plan may only be made upon an event and in a manner consistent with Section 409A of the Code. Should any provision of the Nonqualified Plan, or any other agreement or arrangement contemplated by the Nonqualified Plan or used in conjunction with the Nonqualified Plan be found not to comply with, or otherwise be exempt from, the - 16 - provisions of Section 409A of the Code, such requirements shall be modified and given effect (retroactively if necessary), in the sole discretion of the Committee, in such manner as the Committee determines to be necessary or appropriate to comply with, or to effectuate an exemption from, Section 409A of the Code. If such modification is not possible, any such provision that is not in compliance with Section 409A of the Code shall be deemed ineffective if its application would result in a violation of the requirements set forth in Section 409A of the Code. 6.11. Taxes. The Employer may withhold from any benefit payable under this Plan all federal, state, city, income, employment or other taxes as shall be required pursuant to any law or governmental regulation then in effect. 6.12. Claims Procedure. The Claims Procedure contained in the Qualified Plan shall apply to the Supplement Retirement Benefit payable to a Participant hereunder and is incorporated herein by reference. ARTICLE VII Amendment and Termination 7.1 Amendment and Termination of the Plan. The Employer expects to continue the Nonqualified Plan indefinitely, but specifically reserves the right, in the sole and unfettered discretion of its Board of Directors, at any time, to amend, in whole or in part, any or all of the provision of the Nonqualified Plan and to terminate it in whole or in part, provided that no such amendment or termination may divest any Participant of benefits accrued or earned hereunder prior to the date of any such amendment or termination. - 17 - 7.2. Notice. Notice of the adoption of this Nonqualified Plan and of every Plan amendment shall be given in writing to each Participant and beneficiary of a deceased Participant. NORTHWEST BANK Date: November 19, 2026 By: /s/ Erin F. Siegfried Erin F. Siegfried Chief Legal Counsel 31469920.2

title: XMax Inc.
text: EX-10.1 2 ex10-1.htm EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 Corporate Guarantee Agreement Guarantee Agreement This Guarantee Agreement (this “Agreement”) is made on November 17, 2026 by XMax Inc., tax registration number 90-0746568 and company registration number 3411269, whose principal place of business is 6565 E. Washington Blvd., Commerce, CA 90040 (the “Guarantor” or “XMAX”), for the benefit of kt cloud Co., Ltd., having its principal place of business at The Pinnacle Tower, 343 Hakdong-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea (“kt cloud”, the “Beneficiary” or “KT”). DSH HYPER PTE. LTD., having its principal place of business at 1 Coleman Street, #06-02A, The Adelphi, Singapore 179803 (the “Principal Obligor” or “DSH”) owes certain obligations to KT under certain Upstream Agreement. The Guaranteed Obligations are defined in clause 2 (the “Guarantee”). This Guarantee applies to Guaranteed Obligations arising on or after the effective date of the Upstream Agreement and becomes operative in accordance with clause 9.1. Its terminology does not describe or imply a parent-subsidiary relationship between XMAX and DSH. 1 Parties and commercial basis 1.1 The Guarantor, a Nasdaq-listed company, grants this Guarantee to kt cloud in respect of the Guaranteed Obligations. DSH is not a subsidiary or Affiliate of the Guarantor by virtue of this transaction. Registration, address and notice particulars are recorded in Schedule A. 1.2 DSH contracts with kt cloud under the Master Service Agreement dated October 28, 2026, including its appendices and amendments (the “Upstream Agreement”). The Guarantor purchases the corresponding Services from DSH under the B300 GPUaaS Service Agreement dated October 28, 2026 between DSH and XMax Inc. (the “Service Agreement”). XMax AI Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of the Guarantor, is the Authorized Operator identified under the Service Agreement and uses the Services in that capacity. The Guarantor enters into this Guarantee to enable that use and acknowledges that it derives direct and indirect commercial benefit from the Services and the transactions contemplated by the Upstream Agreement and Service Agreement. kt cloud’s entry into and performance of the Upstream Agreement is consideration for this Guarantee. Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement have the meanings given in the Upstream Agreement, except that “Authorized Operator” has the meaning expressly assigned to XMax AI Inc. in the Service Agreement. Any Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement or in the Upstream Agreement shall have the meanings given in the Service Agreement. 2 Limited guaranteed obligations 2.1 Guaranteed Obligations means only the following amounts payable by Principal Obligor to kt cloud under the Upstream Agreement which have become due and remain unpaid: (a) the monthly Charges set out in Appendix A of the Upstream Agreement for contractually billable Services within the agreed scope, using the fixed Service and Billing Commencement Date of 29 October 2026 under Article 8.6 of the Upstream Agreement (the “Monthly Charges”), together with late interest thereon under Article 8.4 of the Upstream Agreement, provided there shall be no changes to the Charges unless obtaining prior written consent of the Guarantor; (b) the Early Termination Penalty payable by Principal Obligor under Article 11.5 of the Upstream Agreement, but only where (i) the early termination of the Upstream Agreement results from a Service Agreement Default, or (ii) the early termination results from Principal Obligor’s own breach, insolvency or other cause not attributable to Guarantor, kt cloud has first given Guarantor written notice and the opportunity to assume all rights and obligations of Principal Obligor as Customer under the Upstream Agreement in accordance with Article 11.9 of the Upstream Agreement, and Guarantor has not completed the takeover within fifteen (15) calendar days after receipt of such notice, provided kt cloud shall not add any other terms to the novation and the take-over process is simply to replace DSH with Guarantor as agreed in writing on the takeover and treatment of this Guarantee in accordance with clause 9.3; (c) any other amount payable by Principal Obligor to kt cloud under the Upstream Agreement (including damages, indemnities and costs) to the extent arising from a Service Agreement Default; and (d) the reasonable and documented amounts for loss of or damage to the GPU servers, AI Storage or other equipment of kt cloud solely to the extent directly caused by a Service Agreement Default. (e) Notwithstanding the opening words of this clause, Guarantor shall also pay reasonable, documented minimum costs incurred by kt cloud in enforcing this Guarantee in respect of unpaid Guaranteed Obligations, subject to the existing limits and credits in clauses 4 and 6. “Service Agreement Default” means a material breach of the Service Agreement by Guarantor (including non-payment of amounts due from Guarantor, wrongful termination or cancellation by Guarantor, failure by Guarantor to maintain required security, and material breach of applicable use or compliance obligations), including any act or omission of XMax AI Inc. in its capacity as Authorized Operator that constitutes such a material breach by Guarantor, which has not been cured within thirty (30) days after written notice. No breach, insolvency or other default of Principal Obligor shall constitute a Service Agreement Default. XMAX KT Corporate Guarantee | 1 Except for the Guaranteed Obligations expressly described in clause 2.1, Guarantor does not guarantee, and shall have no liability under this Guarantee for, any other obligation, liability or debt of Principal Obligor of any kind, whether under the Upstream Agreement or otherwise, including without limitation: (a) any obligation or liability arising from Principal Obligor’s own breach, negligence, misconduct, insolvency or failure to remit funds; (b) any indemnity given by Principal Obligor under Articles 3.4, 3.7(c), 11.6, 12.4 or 12.6 of the Upstream Agreement, except to the extent directly caused by a Service Agreement Default; (c) any costs and expenses of kt cloud’s termination, disputes or enforcement against Principal Obligor; (d) any Charges for Non-Standard Services, Renewal Terms, capacity or services not covered by the Service Agreement; and (e) any obligation of Principal Obligor to any person other than kt cloud. To the extent of any inconsistency between this Guarantee and Article 9.2, the recitals or any definition of “Guarantor” or “Corporate Guarantee” in the Upstream Agreement, this Guarantee shall prevail, and nothing in the Upstream Agreement shall make Guarantor jointly and severally liable for all obligations of Principal Obligor. 2.2 The Guaranteed Obligations under clause 2.1(a) shall be payable by Guarantor irrespective of whether Principal Obligor’s non-payment results from any Service Agreement Default. The Guaranteed Obligations under clauses 2.1(b), 2.1(c) and 2.1(d) shall be payable only upon satisfaction of the conditions stated in those clauses, and kt cloud’s demand shall identify the relevant Service Agreement Default or the step-in notice and Guarantor’s failure to complete the takeover in accordance with clause 2.1(b)(ii), the original material-default requirement including expiry of thirty (30) days after written notice without cure, as applicable. The Guaranteed Obligations shall not be reduced or affected by (a) the insolvency, dissolution or reorganization of Principal Obligor, or (b) any dispute, set-off or counterclaim between Principal Obligor and Guarantor or any of its Affiliates; provided that any amount paid by Guarantor directly to kt cloud under the Service Agreement payment arrangement shall discharge the corresponding Guaranteed Obligation. 2.3 The definitions, monetary limits and payment credits in clauses 2, 4 and 6 control every provision of this Guarantee, including any undertaking concerning payment or performance, independent indemnity, joint liability, waiver, continuing security, reinstatement or country-specific term. No general wording coverage expands the Guarantee beyond this scope. Any amendment of the Upstream Agreement which increases the Guaranteed Obligations shall bind Guarantor only with Guarantor’s prior written consent; any other amendment, extension or waiver of the Upstream Agreement shall not release, increase or reduce Guarantor’s obligations under this Guarantee. Contracts other than the Upstream Agreement are not covered unless expressly agreed in writing by Guarantor. XMAX KT Corporate Guarantee | 2 3 Guarantee and limited independent indemnity 3.1 Within the limits above in clause 2 and in clause 4, Guarantor irrevocably and unconditionally undertakes, as a primary obligor and not merely as surety, to pay the Guaranteed Obligations directly to kt cloud on kt cloud’s written demand under clause 5. kt cloud need not first sue Principal Obligor, exhaust any other remedy or enforce the SBLC or other security, or establish that Principal Obligor is insolvent or unable to pay. For the amount already paid by SBLC, Kt could shall not make such demand for the same amount under this Agreement. kt cloud may make a demand under clause 5 at any time after any Guaranteed Obligation has remained unpaid for seven (7) calendar days after its Due Date. No demand for the Early Termination Penalty may be made before expiry of the fifteen (15) calendar day takeover period referred to in clause 2.1(b). This is a guarantee of the Guaranteed Obligations only, not a guarantee of all or other debts or obligations under the Upstream Agreement or any other agreements. 3.2 Guarantor separately indemnifies kt cloud against a loss within the definition and only for the coverage of the Guaranteed Obligations if the corresponding guarantee undertaking is unenforceable as a guarantee. This indemnity has exactly the same cause, scope, monetary limits and credits as the guarantee. This indemnity cannot extend to any obligation other than the Guaranteed Obligations, enlarge the recoverable amount or create a second recovery or obligation. Guarantor does not guarantee or undertake Principal Obligor’s non-monetary or other obligations to kt cloud. 4 Principal amount and covered term 4.1 The Principal Limit for the Guaranteed Obligations under clauses 2.1(a), 2.1(b), 2.1(c), 2.1(d) and 2.1(e) is KRW 155,012,298,700, being the total expected monthly Charges under the Upstream Agreement for the Committed Term, exclusive of applicable taxes, subject to approval of that amount by the board of directors of the Guarantor. 4.2 Principal recovery under this Guarantee, including the independent indemnity, may not in aggregate exceed the Principal Limit. For the avoidance of doubt, the Principal Limit shall be reduced by the amount actually paid by Guarantor to kt cloud under this Guarantee Agreement and by all Monthly Charges paid by Guarantor directly to kt cloud on behalf of Principal Obligor under the Service Agreement; any amount paid by Guarantor or XMax AI to Principal Obligor under the Service Agreement shall not reduce the Principal Limit. Late interest under clause 2.1(a) and applicable taxes shall be payable in addition to the Principal Limit. There is no general all-debts undertaking or unrelated-cost indemnity provided by the Guarantor. 4.3 Any agreed change to the value of the Upstream Agreement must be recorded in a signed amount confirmation and a guarantee amendment accepted by kt cloud. Neither Guarantor nor Principal Obligor may unilaterally reduce the stated limit. An increase in capacity, term, amount or scope is not binding under this Guarantee until Guarantor and kt cloud expressly agree to that amendment. 4.4 The covered term is the Committed Term under the Upstream Agreement (currently 29 October 2026 through 28 October 2031, inclusive), as may be adjusted in accordance with the Upstream Agreement and recorded in Schedule A, together with any Service period after the Committed Term as agreed by all parties during which Guaranteed Obligations accrued in respect of the Committed Term remain unpaid. Charges for the initial configuration accrue from the fixed Billing Commencement Date of 29 October 2026 without any separate acceptance testing period; expansion capacity is not billable before it has been supplied and has completed the applicable acceptance testing. XMAX KT Corporate Guarantee | 3 5 Direct demand and payment to kt cloud 5.1 kt cloud’s demand shall be in writing, signed by an authorized signatory of kt cloud, identify this Guarantee and the Upstream Agreement, and state the amount of the Guaranteed Obligations due and unpaid, with copies of the relevant invoices or the calculation of the Early Termination Penalty, after deducting any amounts received by kt cloud for the same obligations (including SBLC proceeds). kt cloud’s demand shall be its conclusive evidence of the amount due, save for manifest error. kt cloud shall send the demand to the Guarantor’s notice address in Schedule A and copy Principal Obligor. 5.2 Guarantor shall pay the amount demanded within 30 days in Seoul after receipt of a demand complying with clause 5.1, directly to kt cloud in KRW in immediately available funds, without any set-off or counterclaim. Guarantor is not required to gross up any payment for tax, and each party shall bear its own bank charges relating to a payment under this Guarantee. Any amount not paid when due shall bear late interest at the rate set forth in Article 8.4 of the Upstream Agreement. kt cloud shall acknowledge receipt and its allocation to the corresponding obligation and provide that record to Principal Obligor and Guarantor. A dispute by Guarantor regarding the amount demanded shall not entitle Guarantor to withhold payment, save in the case of manifest error, and any amount subsequently determined not to have been due shall be refunded by kt cloud. 5.3 If Principal Obligor has already paid kt cloud for the same obligation, that paid portion is no longer unpaid to kt cloud and cannot be collected again under this Guarantee or shall be refund to Guarantor by kt could if it also paid it under this Guarantee. Any corresponding, non-duplicative reimbursement claim among Principal Obligor, Guarantor or XMax AI remains governed by the Service Agreement. 6 No duplicate recovery and retained claims 6.1 kt cloud shall take account of all cleared receipts actually applied to the same Guaranteed Obligations, including payments from Guarantor, Principal Obligor, the SBLC or another source. kt cloud may recover an unpaid balance from Guaranteed Obligations but may not retain more than the actual amount due for the same obligation. Any duplicate receipt shall be promptly reconciled and returned to the Guarantor or credited to the Charges. 6.2 To the extent any Guarantor’s direct payment to kt cloud (including but not limited to Monthly Charges) or its arranged SBLC proceeds discharge a corresponding Principal Obligor upstream liability, Principal Obligor shall credit the corresponding amount in Korean Won against its claim under the Service Agreement against Guarantor, or any corresponding claim it has against XMax AI as Authorized Operator, for the same underlying obligation or loss. The credit shall equal the actual amount in Korean Won paid to kt cloud by the Guarantor. Principal Obligor shall not collect that satisfied portion again as a service charge, termination amount, indemnity, damages or another charge. A demand alone without actual payment does not create a payment credit. For the avoidance of doubt, each payment by Principal Obligor to kt cloud shall, as a matter of contract, automatically and without further action discharge Guarantor’s corresponding obligation under this Agreement. 6.3 Principal Obligor retains recourse under the Service Agreement for the remaining unpaid liability and other recoverable non-duplicative amounts under the Service Agreement after crediting the payments by the Guarantor to kt could. A different cause-of-action label does not permit duplicate recovery. Principal Obligor does not acquire a claim for its own unrelated debt by reason of this Guarantee. Payment of one covered claim in this Agreement releases that claim to the extent paid; it is not a general waiver of Principal Obligor’s retained rights or cancellation of security for other claims under the Service Agreement. XMAX KT Corporate Guarantee | 4 6.4 kt cloud, Principal Obligor and Guarantor shall reconcile payment records and provide reasonable evidence of receipt, allocation and discharge. Credits must be coordinated with ordinary service payments, and any SBLC drawings so that each payment is counted once. 7 Continuing security and release 7.1 This Guarantee is a continuing security for the Guaranteed Obligations arising during the covered term, including any amount becoming due later in respect of that term. Guarantor’s obligations shall not be released, reduced or otherwise affected by any forbearance, time or indulgence granted to Principal Obligor, any amendment, extension or waiver of the Upstream Agreement (subject to clause 2.3), any release, non-enforcement or expiry of the SBLC or any other security, any change in the status, constitution or control of Principal Obligor, XMax AI or Guarantor, the insolvency, liquidation or reorganization of Principal Obligor, or any invalidity or unenforceability of Principal Obligor’s obligations under the Upstream Agreement. 7.2 No unilateral notice of termination releases obligations under the identified covered agreement, including later claims attributable to its covered term. After the Upstream Agreement has expired or been terminated and all Guaranteed Obligations have been finally discharged, kt cloud shall confirm release in writing. In any event, this Guarantee shall automatically terminate and Guarantor shall be released from all obligations hereunder on the date that is twelve (12) months after the expiry or termination of the Upstream Agreement, unless kt cloud has delivered a conforming demand under clause 5 prior to such date in respect of a then-outstanding Guaranteed Obligation. Settlement of one default does not release other unpaid or later covered liabilities. 7.3 If a payment credited against a Guaranteed Obligation is legally avoided or actually returned and the corresponding liability is reinstated, the Guarantee and matching Principal Obligor-Guarantor credit are reinstated or reversed only to that extent, within the original scope and limits. A payment reversal cannot create coverage for any obligation other than the Guaranteed Obligations. 7.4 Subject to any written agreement between kt cloud and Guarantor on the takeover and treatment of this Guarantee in accordance with clause 9.3, Guarantor’s obligations under this Guarantee shall terminate (except for Guaranteed Obligations under clause 2.1(a) accrued for Services actually provided before such termination) upon completion of the takeover in accordance with Article 11.9 of the Upstream Agreement. Termination of the Service Agreement or the Services under it by Principal Obligor does not by itself release Guarantor under this Guarantee, if Guarantor successfully takes over and replaces Principal Obligor under the Upstream Agreement and continues to receive Services directly from kt cloud. If Guarantor assumes the Upstream Agreement, Guarantor shall not be liable under this Guarantee for any Early Termination Penalty or other liability of Principal Obligor, and its obligations shall thereafter be governed solely by the novation agreement. Any direct contract or novation between kt cloud and Guarantor shall be separately agreed in writing. 8 Corporate authority and information 8.1 Guarantor shall provide its signed original Corporate Guarantee Agreement, a copy of the board resolution approving this transaction and the limited scope and amount, no later than 17 November 2026. Guarantor’s obligation to deliver this Guarantee is conditional on approval of its final text and Principal Limit by the board of directors of the Guarantor, and no obligation arises under this Guarantee unless it has been validly executed. It represents that required corporate action has been taken and any necessary approval or filing for execution and performance has been obtained or will be completed as legally required. Guarantor further represents and warrants that this Guarantee constitutes its legal, valid and binding obligation enforceable in accordance with its terms, and that its execution and performance do not conflict with its constitutional documents or any law or agreement binding on it. Guarantor will make disclosure under SEC and Nasdaq rules as necessary. XMAX KT Corporate Guarantee | 5 8.2 The parties will retain the completed anti-money laundry (AML) and end-use records and update material changes. Initial AML and due diligence need not be repeated solely for this Guarantee. Guarantor will maintain its corporate existence and provide reasonable financial or credit information requested for the covered transaction. Neither confidentiality nor a general information covenant expands the liability scope. 9 Effectiveness, law and amendments 9.1 The parties may sign and deliver this Corporate Guarantee Agreement for closing on the later date of the effective date of the Upstream Agreement and Service Agreement, and in any event no later than 17 November 2026. The guarantee undertaking becomes operative and effective on later date of the effective date of the Upstream Agreement and Service Agreement, provided that this completed text has been duly executed by Guarantor and kt cloud. Once operative, this Guarantee covers Guaranteed Obligations under clause 2.1(a) accrued from the fixed Billing Commencement Date of 29 October 2026 and remaining unpaid, notwithstanding its later delivery. Delivery of this Corporate Guarantee Agreement and the verified SBLC remain separate obligations under the revised timetable of the Upstream Agreement. If a Closing Failure (as defined in the Service Agreement) occurs, this Guarantee shall not become operative and Guarantor shall have no liability under it. 9.2 This Guarantee shall be governed by the laws of the Republic of Korea, and the Seoul Central District Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Guarantee. Guarantor irrevocably appoints the process agent identified in Schedule A to receive service of process in the Republic of Korea. Nothing in this clause prevents kt cloud from seeking interim relief in any competent court. 9.3 Notices must be in writing and sent to the agreed addresses in Schedule A. Amendments require authorized signatures of kt cloud and Guarantor and, where Principal Obligor’s rights, credits or liabilities are affected, the authorized signature of Principal Obligor acknowledging and agreeing the affected provisions. Assignment cannot enlarge the Guarantee or deprive Guarantor of its scope limits and credits. Guarantor may not transfer its obligations without kt cloud’s written consent. kt cloud may assign or transfer its rights under this Guarantee together with its rights under the Upstream Agreement without Guarantor’s consent, provided that the assignee shall agree to be bound by terms of this Agreement and Upstream Agreement and continue to provide Services to the Guarantor directly or through Principal Obligor. Invalidity of one provision does not expand the remaining obligations. 9.4 The independent SBLC is governed by its own kt cloud-approved terms. This Guarantee does not amend the bank’s undertaking, expiry, drawing rights or replenishment requirements. Any alignment of SBLC coverage must be expressly agreed with kt cloud and the issuing bank before issuance or amendment. No general statement that in this Agreement constitutes such an amendment to SBLC. 9.5 This Agreement may be executed in three or more counterparts, which together constitute one agreement, and shall become effective when counterparts have been signed by each party and delivered to each other party, subject to the operative date in clause 9.1. The parties need not sign the same counterpart. A signature delivered by facsimile or by email as a PDF has the same force and effect as an original signature page.
